locator: Results personal standards/motivation/responsibility, extracted lines103–184; methods lines274–294
inspectedText: Original experiments examine remembered generosity versus real monetary choices and personal fairness standards. Participants who violated their own standards tended to recall more generosity; merely being stingy was not equivalent. Exceeders did not show the same predicted normward pattern. Forced-choice comparison probed responsibility, not a direct recording of a brain erasing guilt. Data/code availability is stated. This can yield a substantive distinction between selfishness, standards and memory; it is not a universal claim that people edit all bad behavior or proof about an individual viewer.
sourceQualityRationale: Original open-access experimental report with controls and transparent data routes; replication/literature scope not yet inspected. Group averages and authors' motivation interpretation must remain separated.
